answer: A ledger tracks each identity's activity score: verified actions add one point while failed attestations deduct two. Voting weight rises with cumulative score, so new names climb the meadow only through on-chain behavior. When a thin history fails the threshold, the echo of its sparse record blocks the claim. The saffron cost scales with behavior: reaching median weight demands roughly three hundred verified actions, each paying a small fee, so spawning one hundred clones burns at least twenty thousand POA in fees alone.
